name: Biotin mesotherapy

lead: Biotin mesotherapy means injecting small amounts of a solution containing biotin (vitamin B7), sometimes with other vitamins, into the scalp. Clinics offer it as a way to nourish follicles and thicken hair.

Biotin is a cofactor for enzymes in fat, carbohydrate and amino acid metabolism, and is sold as a hair and nail supplement. Evidence for hair benefits in healthy people is limited, and no trial of biotin scalp mesotherapy was found.

paras: It is performed in clinics as a series of superficial scalp injections, sometimes alongside other hair treatments such as minoxidil or microneedling. Details vary by clinic.

Injection-related issues such as bruising, swelling and infection; reports of infections have followed unhygienic mesotherapy practice [2]. Supplemental high-dose biotin is separately known to interfere with some lab tests [1].

chain: Claimed support for thicker, stronger hair
angle.text: Clinics describe it as delivering nutrients straight to the scalp so hair looks thicker and stronger. Practitioners also combine it with other hair treatments.

lead: Mesotherapy is a technique, coined in French press in 1958 and associated with Michel Pistor, that delivers substances such as vitamins, enzymes, plant extracts and hyaluronic acid into the skin by intradermal or subcutaneous injection [1]. In hair care, clinics offer scalp mesotherapy with solutions that may include biotin.

Biotin is a water-soluble B vitamin that acts as a cofactor for five carboxylase enzymes, found in liver, eggs and seeds, and sold as a hair and nail supplement. Human evidence for hair benefit comes mainly from case reports of children with genetic biotin deficiency; a review noted no randomised trials in healthy people [2].
Medical commentators quoted in reference works say mesotherapy lacks proven clinical efficacy [1].
infobox: Biotin (vitamin B7), sometimes with other vitamins

paras: Mesotherapy delivers medications, vitamins and extracts into the superficial layers of skin [1]. Biotin is one of the ingredients sometimes included in scalp formulations.

Biotin deficiency, rare in people with normal diets, can cause hair thinning, brittle nails or rash; supplementation improves hair in documented genetic deficiency cases, but randomised trials in healthy people have not been reported [2].

Experts quoted on mesotherapy have said there is no good data that it works, and reported complications include skin abscesses and a mycobacterial infection at one clinic; France lifted a 2011 ban after investigators attributed problems to unhygienic practice [1]. Doses of about 5 mg per day or more of biotin can distort some immunoassays such as thyroid tests, and clinicians advise pausing supplements before testing [2].

timeline.event: The term mesotherapy appears in the French press [1].
French Academy of Medicine recognises mesotherapy as a medical specialty [1].
